 Women's Rugby League World Cup Australia 34-10 New Zealand: Women’s Rugby League World Cup final – as it happened
 Jillaroos defeat Kiwi Ferns in Brisbane to claim World Cup title and cap dominant tournament
 First-half blitz secures Australia’s fourth straight Women’s Rugby League World Cup title

 1h ago 02.28 EST Summary
 Megan Maurice Well, that probably wasn’t the final scoreline we were expecting after that huge first half, but the Jillaroos will be proud of the fight they showed in difficult circumstances as they dealt with the fatigue arising from the heat and humidity of a November afternoon in Brisbane. It was a valiant effort from both teams in the conditions, but the Jillaroos did the work in the first half to ensure that they came away with the trophy. This is their fourth consecutive World Cup win and they become the first team to win four World Cups.
 The possession finished at 50% each, which shows how much ball New Zealand got in the second half, but they just weren’t able to use it. They will learn a lot from that game and will be stronger for it in the future.
 The Jillaroos were deserving winners after dominating the entire tournament. While it has raised questions about the strength of women’s rugby league across the world, hopefully it entices other nations to begin putting the work into their women’s programs that Australia have done for many years.
 Thanks for joining me this afternoon – there is more rugby league to come with the men’s final kicking off soon. Hop on over to our live blog to keep the rugby league action going!
 Australia v New Zealand: men’s Rugby League World Cup final – live Read more Share 1h ago 02.19 EST Match report
 Relive the excitement of this final in our match report from Angus Fontaine.
 First-half blitz secures Australia’s fourth straight Women’s Rugby League World Cup title Read more Share 1h ago 02.17 EST We’re now hearing from Jillaroos captain Isabelle Kelly.
 “Firstly I just want to thank the Kiwi Ferns, it’s been such a great rivalry for so many years, with so much respect between our teams,” she says. “To my team, I firstly want to thank the girls who didn’t take the field today, you’ve done so much to make sure we got to hold this trophy up today. To Jess and all the girls, this has been my favourite World Cup and I’m so honoured to get to lead this team.”
 View image in fullscreen Isabelle Kelly holds aloft the Women's Rugby League World Cup trophy as the Jillaroos celebrate. Photograph: Cameron Spencer/Getty Images Share Updated at  02.30 EST 1h ago 02.14 EST The Jillaroos are receiving their champions’ medals now from Australian women’s rugby league legend Karyn Murphy.
 View image in fullscreen Winners are grinners. Photograph: Cameron Spencer/Getty Images Share Updated at  02.16 EST 1h ago 02.12 EST The New Zealand captain Georgia Hale is speaking now.
 “Thanks so much to all our fierce and staunch supporters who have been with us for this whole tournament,” she says. “We didn’t quite get the job done today, but the best of the Kiwi Ferns is yet to come, so stay with us.”
 Share 1h ago 02.10 EST Player of the Match: Jaime Chapman
 No great surprises here. Chapman was fantastic with her three tries and so strong under the high balls.
 “Thanks to everyone for coming out,” she says. “Thanks to our Kiwi sisters, you should be proud of yourselves and how you represented your country. To my sisters, I’m so proud of each of you. Thank you to my family, you come to each and every game and I’m so lucky to be surrounded by such great support.”
 View image in fullscreen Player of the match Jaime Chapman celebrates with Tamika Upton. Photograph: Cameron Spencer/Getty Images Share Updated at  02.24 EST 1h ago 02.07 EST Millie Elliott is looking incredibly happy and proud after her final ever professional rugby league game.
 “I grew up playing rugby league as a young girl for the Cobargo Eels. It’s the friendships and the camaraderie of being in a team that I’ve loved the most and will miss the most.”
 Share Updated at  02.13 EST 2h ago 02.03 EST Full time: Australia 34-10 New Zealand
 Despite a lacklustre second half, the Jillaroos still come away with a dominant win in the the World Cup final. The Ferns put up a great fight after the break, but both teams struggled in the heat and there wasn’t a lot of points to be had in the half.
 But the Jillaroos will be celebrating regardless and will be very happy with a strong first half to set up their win.
 View image in fullscreen Kezie Apps is all smiles at full time. Photograph: Andrew Cornaga/AAP Share Updated at  02.14 EST 2h ago 01.58 EST TRY! Australia 34-10 New Zealand (Wiki 69')
 The Ferns were determined to finish with a try and after Kelly loses the ball collecting the kick, Wiki picks it up and dives over the line.
 Share 2h ago 01.56 EST 69 mins: On the wind down now and the Jillaroos finally complete a set – Paki makes a good line break and has Chapman on the outside, but she can’t get the ball away and is pulled down to end the set. The Ferns continue their campaign to try to get some second half points. They’re assisted by a penalty on Apps.
 Share 2h ago 01.54 EST 67 mins: A little break as Nicholls falls to the ground clutching her hamstring. A disappointing end to her World Cup campaign. The Ferns look like they may score after a great fifth tackle kick and receive and some great passing, but Kelly pulls out a brilliant try-saving tackle.
 Share 2h ago 01.51 EST 65 mins: A big carry and some strong post-contact metres from Biddle on the third tackle for the Ferns. They try to make a big last tackle play, but they can’t get a kick away and the Jillaroos shut them down. Once again they can’t quite complete their set on the last tackle – Southwell makes a good line break and flicks the ball out to Apps, but she can’t control it.
 Share 2h ago 01.49 EST 63 mins: The Ferns complete their set and Upton picks up the kick and runs it. They nearly complete their set, but there’s another forward pass called on the last tackle and hand the ball back over to the Ferns – they’ve now made nine errors in the second half.
 Share 2h ago 01.47 EST 61 mins: Sergis makes a strong line break and gets the Jillaroos back on track. But soon after, the referee rules a forward pass and we have another change of possession. It’s been quite a while since we’ve had a completed set. The Ferns take the scrum feed and march on down the field.
 Share 2h ago 01.45 EST 59 mins: An error from Church gives the ball back to the Ferns, but a couple of tackles later, Biddle makes an error as well. We take a quick break with a head clash between Taufa and McGregor. Taufa gets taped up on the field, while McGregor heads off for a HIA. The Jillaroos get the scrum feed, but Aiken immediately loses the ball. The Ferns then lose the ball a few tackles later. The wheels are falling off both teams now.
 Share 2h ago 01.41 EST 57 mins: The Ferns start with the ball after the break and play a decent set, but there’s no contest on the kick receive – they need to put more pressure on at this stage of the game.
 Share 2h ago 01.38 EST We’re taking a drinks break now – both teams will be happy for this reprieve from the stifling heat and humidity.
 View image in fullscreen Sariah Paki of Australia is tackled by three Ferns players. Photograph: Cameron Spencer/Getty Images Share Updated at  01.52 EST 2h ago 01.37 EST 55 mins: The Ferns get a penalty for Chapman being offside and they have a huge opportunity now. The Jillaroos defence is unbreakable, they are so strong and determined, wrapping them up ball and all to stop the offloads. The Jillaroos get the ball from their 20m line after the kick goes dead in goal and get on the attack.
 Share 2h ago 01.35 EST 53 mins: Some great footwork and offloading from the Jillaroos as they get close to the line. Penitani Gray is ruled to knock the ball on in the tackle – the Jillaroos challenge but finally they get one wrong and the Ferns get the scrum feed. A great line break from Nicholl gets them down the field and there are some huge try-saving tackles on the line from Kelly and Chapman.
 Share 2h ago 01.32 EST 51 mins: Southwell finishes the Jillaroos’ set with an absolutely fantastic kick that settles right down in the corner of the field. But Southwell undoes her good work by giving away a penalty for crowding in the tackle. And then Waaka loses in the ball in the tackle on the first play. The heat may be starting to get to both teams now.
 Share 2h ago 01.30 EST 49 mins: A scrum feed from the Ferns 10m out and they have the opportunity to score the first points of the half. The Jillaroos hold a strong line and make it very difficult. The Ferns get a kick through the line, which is taken by Upton and she does very well to get back into the field of play.
 Share 2h ago 01.29 EST 47 mins: Chapman fields the bomb from Kiria-Ratu with ease and the Jillaroos look to get down the field and score their first points in the second half. But the Ferns hold them down in their own half in a good defensive display. They follow it up with strong counterattack – they’re looking better in this half and appear to have plenty of fight left in them. McGregor puts up a brilliant kick, Church comes down with it, but loses it in the tackle.
 Share 2h ago 01.26 EST 45 mins: Another successful captain’s challenge from the Jillaroos – Belinda Sharpe is sure she’s going to catch them in a genuine knock on one of these times, but it hasn’t happened yet. A big line break from Kernick, but her pass can’t find Apps and the Ferns dive on it. Waaka tries some fancy footwork to break through the line, but the defence is too strong.
 Share 2h ago 01.23 EST 43 mins: Another strong set from the Jillaroos that finished with a good kick from Southwell, who threads it through, but Kelly gives away a penalty with a high tackle on the kick receive. Penitani Gray then gives away another and ends up on report for a dangerous tackle.
 Share 2h ago 01.21 EST 41 mins: Aiken nearly dives over the line, but is held up in a brilliant try-saving tackle by Nicholl. It’s a good set for the Ferns, finished with a spiralling kick that Church controls with her foot and guides over to Upton.
 Share 2h ago 01.19 EST 39 mins: Church makes another great line break, offloads to Bent, who gets it to Aiken for a deft little kick. The Ferns are forced into a line drop out and it’s another attacking set for the Jillaroos.
 View image in fullscreen Abbi Church dives for the ball over Mele Hufanga. Photograph: Darren England/AAP Share Updated at  01.49 EST 2h ago 01.17 EST 37 mins: Sergis nearly comes up with the ball from the kick off, but the Ferns grab it and make their way down field. Plenty of great offloads nearly gets them down to the try line, but they put up a kick and Sergis collects it, makes a great run, then there’s an intercept from the Ferns, then they lose the ball, the Jillaroos pick it up again and the referee rules a double knock on, with the Jillaroos getting the first touch. They again challenge it and are successful, so get the ball back on their own 20m line.
 Share 2h ago 01.14 EST Second half begins
 The Jillaroos have kicked off and the second half is underway!
 Share Updated at  01.49 EST 2h ago 01.09 EST Taking a look at some stats now – the Jillaroos have had 58% of the possession, which isn’t miles more than the Ferns, but they have done so much more with it. Australia lead the run metres 882m to 384m, which is very telling. The Australian women also have seven line breaks to one and 21 tackle breaks to four, so it has been very hard for the Ferns to match it considering their solid, but not amazing sets. They’ll work hard to try to reverse some of these stats in the second half.
 Share 3h ago 01.01 EST Half time: Australia 34-6
 A hugely dominant half for the Jillaroos, who have put their heart and soul into this match so far and are desperate to take home this World Cup. Chapman starred with three tries in the half, equalling the record for most tries in a tournament. Speaking at the break, she was confident in her team’s ability to close this match out in the second half.
 “I am happy with how we are going but we still have another half, we’ll be ready to come back out,” she said. “It is so humid and hot. It feels like Bali, I’m going there next week! It’s good on the lungs but we are fitter and stronger and we’ll come out in the second half and go again.”
 The Kiwi Ferns haven’t been playing badly, but they just haven’t been at the same level as the Jillaroos. There haven’t been too many errors, but they aren’t able to match the dynamism and flair of the Australians so far. But with the extended half time break and a bit of a rev up, they may be able to turn this around and have a strong second half.
 Share 3h ago 00.56 EST 35 mins: Just 30 seconds before half time for the Jillaroos to try to add to their score and they immediately pick up a penalty and take a quick tap. They get another penalty for a late hit on the kicker, but they opt not to make another run and Southwell flops on the ground to take us to half time.
 View image in fullscreen Jesse Southwell weaves through traffic in the first half. Photograph: Darren England/AAP Share Updated at  01.15 EST 3h ago 00.54 EST GOAL! Australia 34-6 New Zealand (Southwell 34')
 Upton has made this one nice and easy for Southwell and she adds the two points.
 Share 3h ago 00.53 EST TRY! Australia 32-6 New Zealand (Upton 32')
 The Ferns take the scrum feed 40m out from Australia’s line and push down the field. An offload to McGregor gets her into some space, she passes to Waaka who drops the ball and the Jillaroos are back on the attack. A good line break from Southwell gets them into strong field position and then Church and Upton combine on the wing for a little give and go to put Upton over – running across to put the ball down near the uprights.
 View image in fullscreen Tamika Upton evades a tackle from Leianne Tufuga. Photograph: Patrick Hamilton/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  01.36 EST 3h ago 00.50 EST 31 mins: Another challenging kick for Southwell, but she can’t slot this one and it hits the post. The Jillaroos start another set, but lose the ball through an incorrect play the ball.
 Share 3h ago 00.48 EST TRY! Australia 28-6 New Zealand (Chapman 28')
 A huge line break from Chapman sees her power down the field past the defence and gets her third try of the match!
 View image in fullscreen Jaime Chapman scores once more. Photograph: Patrick Hamilton/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  01.03 EST 3h ago 00.47 EST 29 mins: The Ferns start the set deep in their own half, but they look determined and are making some good post-contact metres and looking for offloads. A really nice kick from Kiria-Ratu finds Waaka, who offloads the ball. There is a knock on ruled against Australia, but a captain’s challenge finds that they did not in fact touch the ball and we go back to the previous play the ball. The Ferns put up a bomb that is taken well by Aiken.
